items.t: WIG20 closes at 4,279.50 points, up 1.69 percent
sum: The WIG20 closed Thursday's session on November 12, 2026, at 4,279.50 points, up 1.69 percent from the previous session. The move came as Warsaw equities continued their recovery, although the late-day performance took place against a less supportive tone in US markets. The closing level and daily change were reported by Polish Press Agency.

Allegro was the strongest WIG20 component, rising 5.09 percent during the session. According to XYZ, the e-commerce group published third-quarter results ahead of the Thursday opening that exceeded analyst expectations and raised its 2026 forecasts. The company reported revenue of PLN 3.4 billion, adjusted EBITDA of PLN 1.1 billion and net income attributable to the parent company's shareholders of PLN 574.7 million for the quarter.

Allegro now expects Polish GMV to rise by about 13 percent in 2026 and group adjusted EBITDA to increase by 22 to 24 percent. The guidance update also reflected a new logistics agreement with InPost. The agreement runs through December 31, 2031, according to the same report. Other strong performers included PGE, Alior Bank, Orlen and Tauron.

The session was not uniformly positive. KGHM fell 1.28 percent and Kruk declined 1.31 percent, making them the weakest WIG20 constituents alongside Budimex, Pekao and Zabka. The WIG-Mining sector lost 1.17 percent, while the WIG-Energy index gained 4.28 percent. The market backdrop therefore favored energy stocks and selected banks, but weakness in copper prices weighed on mining exposure.

Investors now turn to Friday's Polish data calendar. Preliminary third-quarter GDP figures and full October inflation data are scheduled for November 13, alongside balance-of-payments figures from the National Bank of Poland. These releases may provide a new test for the recovery in Polish large-cap equities after Thursday's broad-based advance.

items.t: BHP (ASX:BHP) Share Price: KGHM Pact, Faraday Stake and Escondida Concentrator Funding in Focus
WIG 20 at 4,155.71 Points as Warsaw Rebounds at Midday
sum: The WIG 20 was trading at 4,155.71 points at 13:03 Berlin time on Monday, November 9, according to the GPW Benchmark. The Warsaw blue-chip index was up 0.59% from Friday's close of 4,131.37 points, leaving the current session in progress rather than representing a final close.

The WIG 20 opened at 4,140.17 points and traded between 4,123.36 and 4,178.75 points during the session covered by the official index page. Friday's decline had taken the benchmark down 1.85%, according to the Polish Press Agency, making Monday's advance a partial recovery rather than a full reversal of the previous session's move.

Business Insider Polska reported at 13:06 Berlin time that the WIG 20 was at 4,155.64 points, up 0.59%. It said Modivo was gaining more than 3%, while mBank, Budimex and KGHM were each up more than 2%; Pepco was the only clearly weaker WIG 20 constituent highlighted, down about 2%.

The market was also digesting Friday's decision by S&P Global Ratings to revise Poland's sovereign outlook to negative from stable. S&P affirmed the foreign-currency ratings at A-/A-2 and lowered the local-currency ratings to A-/A-2 from A/A-1, citing fiscal deficits, rising debt and political constraints on consolidation. The rating action is a dated macroeconomic development, not a new Monday index event.

The broader backdrop was more supportive. Saxo reported stronger Asian equities and higher U.S. futures after Friday's technology rebound. It also identified Tuesday's U.S. consumer-price report as the next major macro test, while expectations for Federal Reserve policy remained sensitive to stronger employment data.
Further WIG 20 developments can be followed on the WIG 20 topic page.

items.t: WIG 20 closes 0.46 percent higher at 4,209.15 points
sum: The WIG 20 ended Thursday's session at 4,209.15 points, up 0.46 percent from the previous close, according to ISBnews. The close followed a second consecutive advance for Warsaw's blue-chip index, but the wider market moved in the opposite direction: the WIG fell 0.07 percent, while the mWIG40 and sWIG80 declined 1.62 percent and 1.00 percent, respectively.

Selected consumer companies and banks provided the main support. A WNP report citing PAP said LPP, Dino Polska and Modivo were among the stronger consumer names during the session. LPP had reported estimated third-quarter sales growth of 20 percent in constant currencies, while comparable-store sales increased 4.4 percent.

Bank stocks also contributed to the advance. PKO BP rose after reporting third-quarter 2026 net profit of PLN 2,933 million, up from PLN 2,837 million a year earlier and 4.1 percent above analysts' expectations, according to the same report. Selected other banks also gained, although the sector's performance remained mixed.

The positive performance of the WIG 20 did not reflect the broader trading session. ISBnews reported that 113 stocks rose on the Warsaw Stock Exchange, 220 declined and 69 were unchanged. Within the blue-chip index, KGHM and Allegro were among the notable decliners. KGHM fell after returning to losses, while Allegro also weakened following a strong run in previous weeks.

Energy shares were mixed to firmer in the session. PGE and Tauron gained, while PGE also announced a PLN 3.89 billion term-loan agreement with a banking consortium to finance or refinance investment spending related to a gas-fired power plant in Rybnik. This company-specific development was reported in the market coverage and is not, by itself, evidence of a broader index trend.

The WNP report quoted Noble Securities analyst Mateusz Chrzanowski as linking the improved mood in Warsaw to greater risk appetite after the US elections and to easing concerns about risks connected with the Iran conflict. He also pointed to lower commodity prices and their possible effect on inflation expectations. At the same time, the report noted that expectations for lower interest-rate pressure could offset some of the benefit for banks.

items.t: WIG20 closes at 4,209.15 points, up 0.46%
WIG 20 closes at 4,190.08 points, up 1.24 percent
sum: The WIG 20 ended Wednesday's session, November 4, at 4,190.08 points, up 1.24 percent from the previous close. The closing figure and daily move were reported by Polish Press Agency and are consistent with the closing data carried by ISBnews on Investing.com.

The move followed a weaker previous session, when the index closed at 4,138.60 points on November 3. Wednesday's gain therefore restored some of the ground lost at the start of the week. The broader WIG index rose 1.47 percent to 158,141.27 points, while the mWIG40 gained 2.30 percent to 10,728.30 points and the sWIG80 added 0.41 percent to 29,465.46 points, according to the ISBnews closing report.

Market leadership was concentrated in selected commodity-sensitive and state-controlled names. Business Insider Polska reported that KGHM was among the strongest WIG 20 constituents during the session, supported by higher copper, silver and gold prices. Shares of state-owned energy companies also advanced in the report's intraday account. Those observations help explain the sectoral backdrop, but do not by themselves establish that any single stock caused the index's full-day performance.

Equity turnover on the Warsaw market amounted to PLN 2.803 billion. PKO Bank Polski generated the highest turnover at PLN 416.21 million. Across the GPW, 200 stocks rose, 122 declined and 80 were unchanged, indicating a broadly positive session rather than a gain limited to a narrow group of index heavyweights.

The close came against an international backdrop shaped by reactions to the US midterm election result and stronger Asian markets. For investors, the session showed a recovery in Polish large caps, but the next direction will still depend on commodity prices, global risk appetite and domestic political developments. Further index coverage is available on the WIG 20 topic page.

items.t: WIG 20 closes at 4,138.60 points, down 0.34 percent
WIG 20 falls 1.36% to 4,095.98 points at midday
sum: The WIG 20 came under renewed pressure during Tuesday's session, extending its decline toward the 4,100-point level. According to Puls Biznesu, the index stood at 4,095.98 points at 12:51 Berlin time on November 3, 2026, down 1.36% from the previous close.

The weakness was concentrated in several heavily weighted large-cap names. Allegro was down 4.20%, KGHM fell 3.80% and LPP declined 3.48% in the GPW market snapshot at 12:35. Bank stocks were mixed: mBank lost 2.16%, while Pekao gained 0.67% and Alior rose 0.15%. Tauron, up 1.53%, was among the strongest WIG 20 constituents.

The intraday market pattern was consistent with a broader risk-off tone in Europe. Parkiet reported that the selling pressure had shifted from banks, which had weighed on the market during the previous two sessions, toward KGHM, Allegro and LPP. The publication also noted that the WIG 20 had moved below mid-October lows, bringing the index closer to a technical support area from early October.

Positive company news offered only limited support. Tauron gained after reporting estimated third-quarter EBITDA of PLN 1,821 million and revenue of PLN 8,624 million, above market expectations of PLN 1,565 million and PLN 7,721 million, respectively, according to Parkiet. Eurocash also reported figures above expectations, but the strength in those shares was not enough to offset the declines among several larger index members.

Market sentiment was also shaped by caution ahead of the US midterm elections. Forsal cited an analyst view that investors could reduce portfolio risk before the election outcome and the expected changes in the US Congress. European index futures were also weaker in the morning, adding to the cautious backdrop for Warsaw equities.

The WIG 20's move below 4,100 points marks a clear deterioration from Monday's close at 4,152.65 points. Whether the early-October support area attracts buyers will depend on sentiment in global markets and on the reaction to the US election results. This is an assessment of market conditions, not an investment recommendation.
Further WIG 20 coverage is available on the WIG 20 topic page.

items.t: WIG 20 closes at 4,152.65 points, down 0.68%
WIG 20 falls 0.73% to 4,150.53 in midday trading
sum: The WIG 20 was trading at 4,150.53 points at 12:53 Warsaw time on Monday, November 2, according to Puls Biznesu. That represented a decline of 0.73% from Friday's close at 4,180.88 points, a level also reported in the morning market review by BNP Paribas. The Warsaw session was still in progress, so the reading was an intraday level rather than a closing value.

Trading remained defensive across the largest Polish shares. Rzeczpospolita reported that banks were among the weakest WIG 20 constituents, while CD Projekt, Modivo, PZU and KGHM also faced selling pressure. Dino and Allegro were among the shares showing relative strength. The report described the market reaction to the latest political tensions as cautious rather than disorderly.

At the broader market level, the WIG was down 0.90% at 156,256.91 points at 12:38, while the mWIG40 had fallen 1.25% to 10,543.53 points. The figures underline that the weakness was not limited to the WIG 20, although the index's heavy bank weighting made it particularly sensitive to pressure on financial stocks.

Market commentary linked the subdued tone to the weekend escalation of a dispute surrounding Poland's Constitutional Tribunal, which increased uncertainty over domestic institutions and policy conditions. WNP also cited weaker global sentiment following disappointing technology-company results as a factor discussed by market analysts. Those concerns followed Friday's broad sell-off, when the WIG 20 lost 2.40%.

Investors were also looking ahead to the US session. The BNP Paribas morning review identified the final US manufacturing PMI and the ISM manufacturing index as later-day data points, while Apple and Palantir were due to report after the close of Wall Street. In Poland, the published calendar listed the October industrial PMI and company-specific meetings and dividend events, but no single scheduled item that by itself defined the WIG 20's midday direction.

For investors, the intraday picture pointed to continued sensitivity to bank performance, domestic political headlines and global technology risk. The index had not yet produced a confirmed close, leaving the final session result open to changes in the afternoon. Further coverage of the WIG 20 is available on the topic page.

items.t: WIG 20 falls 1.3 percent as banks and KGHM slide
sum: WIG 20 was down 54 points, or 1.3 percent, at 4,213 points at 12:02 p.m. CEST on October 22, 2026, as banks and KGHM weakened. Polish retail sales rose 3.3 percent year over year in September, below the 6.9 percent consensus, XTB reported.

Since the 4,168-point midday level, WIG 20 has recovered 45 points. Pepco rose 1.6 percent after the company announced a new multiyear share-buyback program, while KGHM remained the weakest blue chip, PAP reported.

Bank stocks and energy shares were among the weakest groups in Warsaw. KGHM fell 2.8 percent, while PKO BP and Pekao each lost about 2.0 percent, according to PAP. The selling followed Wednesday's record close, when WIG 20 reached 4,267 points.
- Pepco up 1.6 percent: shares advanced after a new buyback program was announced.
- KGHM down 2.8 percent: the copper producer extended its recent decline.
- PKO BP down 2.0 percent: bank shares weakened with the sector.
- Pekao down 2.0 percent: the stock followed the broader bank-sector decline.

items.t: EU grants strategic status to $2.4bn KGHM copper projects
sum: The European Commission has designated two major investments by Polish copper producer KGHM Polska Miedz as strategic projects under the EU's Critical Raw Materials Act (CRMA), the company said on Friday, as the bloc races to diversify supply chains and reduce reliance on China.
The projects, worth a combined 9.5-billion zlotys ($2.44-billion), aim to strengthen Europe's copper mining and recycling capacity and reduce dependence on non-EU suppliers.
The Retków-Grodziszcze mining project aims to extract more than 100-million tons of ore by 2055, yielding nearly 1.5-million tons of copper and over 5 000 tons of silver.
KGHM will also transform its Legnica smelter into a recycling facility with an expected annual production of about 135 000 tons of electrolytic copper and 250 tons of nickel.
The designation could provide both projects with streamlined permitting, better administrative coordination and access to preferential financing.

Michal Kozak, an analyst at Polish brokerage Trigon, told Reuters the designation was "directionally good news" for KGHM but cautioned that it was unclear whether it would lead to significant financial support.
The investments align with the bloc's Critical Raw Materials Act, which aims for recycling to account for at least 25% of the EU's annual consumption of strategic raw materials.

items.t: EU puts KGHM’s $2.4B copper projects on fast track
KGHM launched USD 725 million expansion and KGHM stock gains 4.37 percent
sum: KGHM (ISIN PLKGHM000017) was trading at EUR 78.26 at Lang & Schwarz on October 9, 2026 at 11:15 a.m. CEST, up 4.37 percent versus the prior close of EUR 74.98. The company launched a USD 725 million expansion of its Sierra Gorda mine in Chile on October 2, 2026, according to KGHM.

On July 30, 2026, KGHM released second-quarter results showing revenue of USD 3,488.90 million, up 51.80 percent year over year, and net profit of USD 557.10 million, up 738.50 percent, as reported by Frontier.
On October 2, 2026, KGHM management said the company was pursuing an acquisition process and described a potential USD 1.00 billion plus copper project as an ideal target, according to Biznes24.

On October 2, 2026, the Sierra Gorda expansion became the latest concrete investment milestone. KGHM owns 55.00 percent of the mine, while South32 owns 45.00 percent, and the project is scheduled to reach full production capacity in the second half of 2030, according to KGHM.

The fourth grinding line is designed to lift annual ore processing capacity from 48 million to 60 million tonnes and copper production by 20.00 percent. Completion is scheduled for the end of 2029, with the project financed through operating cash flow and available debt instruments.

The investment gives the strong second-quarter figures a longer operating link, but it also increases the importance of execution and copper prices. Frontier reported that second-quarter EBITDA reached USD 1,010.90 million, up 216.80 percent year over year, while the EBITDA margin rose to 29.00 percent from 13.90 percent.

KGHM's next substantiated reporting date is November 18, 2026, when it plans to publish its consolidated third-quarter report, according to the company's investor-relations page. The other dated project milestone is the second half of 2030, when Sierra Gorda is scheduled to reach full production capacity.

items.t: BHP–KGHM copper alliance: exploration and project-screening notes for engineers
European shares muted as oil rally fuels caution; Novartis tumbles
sum: EUROPEAN shares were little changed on Tuesday (Sep 8) as escalating tensions in the Middle East and rising oil prices kept investors cautious, while Novartis suffered its steepest one-day decline on record after reporting a second setback in its drug pipeline.
The pan-European Stoxx 600 was down 0.05 per cent at 649.6. Switzerland’s benchmark index fell 1.6 per cent, weighed down by Novartis, which slid 10.9 per cent.

Novartis was the biggest faller on the Stoxx 600 after the Swiss drugmaker said its experimental treatment for a muscle-wasting disorder had failed in a late-stage trial. The news came a day after the company disclosed that an experimental cholesterol drug had also failed a closely watched late-stage study.

Energy shares gained 0.6 per cent as Brent crude futures hovered around US$98 a barrel. Oil prices rose after Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi forces attacked energy facilities and cities in Saudi Arabia, underscoring the risk that the conflict could spread further across the region and disrupt fuel supplies to global markets.
Mining stocks also advanced as copper prices climbed. Boliden, Antofagasta and KGHM gained between 4.6 per cent and 6.3 per cent, while the broader European mining index jumped 2 per cent.

On the economic front, German exports unexpectedly fell in July, with weaker shipments to European Union countries and China highlighting the fragility of the trade-driven recovery in Europe’s largest economy.

Elevated oil prices have revived inflation concerns, contributing to a recent global bond selloff and strengthening expectations that central banks may need to keep monetary policy restrictive for longer.

items.t: BHP, KGHM join forces in global hunt for copper
KGHM signs MoU with BHP to explore areas of mutual interest including exploration & development projects
Polish copper giant KGHM partners with BHP
Novartis Plunges Over 10% on Second Drug Setback; European Stocks Waver Near Elevated Oil Prices
sum: Swiss pharmaceutical giant Novartis suffered its second consecutive drug trial setback on the 8th, with its muscle-wasting disease candidate "del-desiran" failing to meet endpoints in a late-stage clinical trial. The stock plunged more than 10%, marking the largest single-day decline in the company's history and dragging the Swiss benchmark index down 1.6%. European equities closed slightly lower the same day amid Middle East tensions and elevated oil prices, with the pan-European STOXX 600 index edging down 0.05% to close at 649.60 points.

Escalating Middle East tensions dominated the session. The Iran-backed Houthi group in Yemen launched attacks on Saudi Arabian energy facilities and cities, raising concerns that a wider conflict could disrupt global fuel supplies. Brent Crude futures climbed to near $98 per barrel (approximately NT$3,100), with persistently high energy prices reigniting inflation worries and fueling the recent sell-off in global bond markets.

Energy and mining stocks were direct beneficiaries of rising oil and copper prices. The pan-European energy sector rose 0.6%, while mining stocks surged 2%. Swedish mining and smelting company Boliden jumped 6.3%, Chilean copper miner Antofagasta gained 4.7%, and Polish copper producer KGHM posted similarly strong gains. In the UK market, oil major BP rose 0.7%, while Shell advanced 0.5%.

Novartis's plunge was the day's biggest story. The company announced that its experimental drug "del-desiran," developed for muscle-wasting disease, failed to meet primary endpoints in a late-stage clinical trial. This marked the second consecutive day of drug development setbacks for Novartis — the previous day, its closely watched cholesterol-lowering drug "pelacarsen" also failed to reduce the risk of heart attacks and strokes in a pivotal trial.

The market reaction was severe, with Novartis shares tumbling 10.9% in a single session. The stock was not only the worst performer in the pan-European STOXX 600 index but also set a new record for the largest single-day decline since the company's listing. The Swiss SMI index fell between 1.55% and 1.6% as a result, making it the weakest performer among major European indices.

items.t: Daily Summary: Dollar Recovers Losses, Oil Near 3-Week Highs 🗽 US30 Falls 1%
sum: - Thursday’s Wall Street session is also bringing moderate declines, led by the Dow Jones Industrial Average as Walmart shares fall more than 8% after earnings. US30 futures are down close to 1%, the S&P 500 is lower by 0.55%, while the Nasdaq 100 is down more than 0.7%.

- Investors are being unsettled by a stronger U.S. dollar and rebounding Treasury yields, which are erasing a large part of yesterday’s decline triggered by the U.S. Treasury Department’s intervention in the bond market. Brent crude futures (OIL) are trading above $93.5 per barrel, the highest level since July 24.

- SpaceX shares are drawing attention with a decline of more than 6%. Moderna shares are down 25% after yesterday’s surge of more than 100%, which followed reports of encouraging results from the mRNA cancer therapy the company is developing together with Merck.

- U.S. data generally point to a still-solid labor market and stronger manufacturing activity. Initial jobless claims fell to 206,000 versus 210,000 expected, although continuing claims rose to 1.799 million compared with the 1.788 million forecast. The Philadelphia Fed Business Index jumped to 47.4 from 41.4, clearly beating the consensus estimate of 25 and confirming strong manufacturing activity. In addition, the CB Leading Index rose 0.2% MoM versus 0.1% expected and a previous decline of 0.2%. Taken together, these data do not give the Fed a clear argument for rapid policy easing.

- Fed’s Alberto Musalem does not want to pre-judge the Federal Reserve’s decision at the September meeting and stressed that he does not currently have a strong view on the direction of the next move. He noted, however, that core inflation should be taken into account during supply shocks and that raising rates earlier could reduce the need for even stronger tightening later. In his view, reaching the 2% inflation target is less likely at the current level of rates, which gives his comments a cautious and slightly hawkish tone.

- The 30-year TIPS auction was fairly strong. The 2.973% yield came in below the 2.991% WI level, while the bid-to-cover ratio rose to 2.82 and the share of so-called indirect bidders reached 84.4%, pointing to solid demand from large investors.

items.t: Azimut Exploration Stock: A Partner-Funded Nickel Hunt After a 19.6% Nickel Hit
Copper, Not Gold, Is the Real Driver Behind the Mining Stock Surge
Azimut and KGHM Launch 2026 Campaign at Kukamas
sum: 5,000 metres of drilling to expand the high-grade Nickel-PGE Perseus Zone

LONGUEIL, Quebec, July 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Azimut Exploration Inc. ("Azimut" or the "Company") (TSXV: AZM) (OTCQX: AZMTF) is pleased to announce that a comprehensive partner-funded exploration program is commencing on the Kukamas Property (the "Property") in the Eeyou Istchee James Bay ("James Bay") region of Quebec, Canada.

The Property is subject to an option agreement with KGHM International Ltd ("KGHM"). KGHM has earned a 50% interest in the Property and has elected to enter the second option phase to earn an additional 20% interest upon delivery of a preliminary economic assessment. Azimut remains the operator of the 2026 program.
The $3.4-million work program will be deployed over the two (2) blocks of the Property (see Figures 1 to 4):
- Priority is given to the advancement of the high-grade nickel-PGE (platinum group element) Perseus discovery through the following work:
- An induced polarization ("IP") survey over the komatiite sequence hosting the mineralized zone to identify its footprint and generate new drilling targets (completed, see below).
- 5,000 metres of diamond drilling, mostly dedicated to expanding Perseus.

items.t: Top 10 Copper-producing Companies
sum: The top 10 biggest copper-mining companies include BHP, Codelco and Freeport-McMoran. Learn about the operations of the top copper producers here.
Copper miners with productive assets have much to gain as supply and demand tighten and prices soar.
The price of copper reached new all-time highs in 2026 on both the COMEX in the United States and the London Metals Exchange (LME) in the United Kingdom, maintaining copper's momentum in 2025.

They first set record highs on January 29 of US$6.61 per pound on the COMEX and US$14,527.50 per metric ton on the LME. On May 13, the COMEX price surpassed its January peak, hitting a new all-time high of US$6.71.
Another trend driving future copper demand is the rapid urbanization in the Global South, as rural populations migrate to cities, putting pressure on electricity grids.

Due to the challenges associated with finding, developing, permitting and mining copper deposits, the higher demand is being met by slow growth of new supply. Mines that are in operation tend to be quite large and operate for decades as copper producers concentrate on mine expansions and brownfield projects aimed at extending mine lifetimes.
Given those factors, investors interested in copper should keep an eye on the world’s top copper miners and their operations.

items.t: Lumina–KGHM copper supply talks: project scale and offtake lens for mine planners
sum: Newly listed Lumina Metals has signed a letter of intent with KGHM to negotiate technical and commercial terms for future copper concentrate supply from its 120 sq. km Nowa Sól underground copper-silver project in Poland’s Northern copper belt. The project, adjacent to KGHM’s existing copper-silver mines and processing facilities, hosts a measured and indicated resource of 604 million tonnes grading 1.24% copper and 38 g/t silver from over 51,000 metres of drilling. Lumina raised C$406.2 million in its TSX IPO, is targeting a Warsaw listing, and is currently trading around C$11.50 per share.
- Letter of intent with KGHM specifically targets future copper concentrate offtake, not joint venture ownership.
- Proximity to KGHM’s existing copper-silver mines allows potential tie-in to established processing and smelting infrastructure.
- Nowa Sól lies in Poland’s Lubuskie Region within the Northern copper belt, a mature mining district.
- Discovery dates back to 2014, giving roughly a decade of geological work and data acquisition.
- Over 51,000 m of drilling underpins the current resource model and mine planning assumptions.
- KGHM’s adjacent operations are currently Poland’s only copper-silver producers, centralising regional processing options.

items.t: Newly listed Lumina in talks with Poland’s KGHM over potential supply deal
sum: Newly listed Lumina Metals (TSX: LMCU) says it has entered talks with Polish mining giant KGHM over a potential supply deal involving the company’s flagship copper project.

In a press release on Tuesday, the Canadian miner said it has signed a letter of intent with KGHM to discuss technical and commercial terms related to the future supply of copper concentrates from its Nowa Sól project.

Nowa Sól represents a major underground project covering 120 sq. km of Poland’s Northern copper belt. It is situated near KGHM’s existing copper-silver mine operations, which constitute Poland’s only producers of the metals and host one of Europe’s key copper processing facilities.

The letter with KGHM, says Lumina’s CEO Jordan Pandoff, represents an “important step in reinforcing the Polish metal mining industry” and in advancing the company’s strategy to position Nowa Sól as “a cornerstone of copper and silver supply” within both Poland and the European Union.

“We are delighted to open discussions with KGHM, a globally recognized European leader in copper mining and smelting, as we continue to advance the project toward development leveraging Polish local content of the highest quality,” he added.

Since its initial discovery in 2014, Lumina has completed over 51,000 metres of drilling, from which it outlined a measured and indicated resource of 604 million tonnes grading 1.24% copper and 38 g/t silver. This resource, according to the company, makes Nowa Sól one of the world’s most significant undeveloped copper projects and one of the largest undeveloped silver projects.

To advance the project further, Lumina recently completed an initial public offering of its common stock on the Toronto Stock Exchange, raising C$406.2 million ($297 million). The company also said it plans to list its stock on the Warsaw exchange.

items.t: Largest Silver Mining Companies and Producers
Poland’s Wild Stock Market Is Europe’s Best Kept Secret: Here’s the ETF to Play The Run
sum: This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.

Most European equity exposure sits in Western Europe: Germany, France, the UK. Poland, the largest economy in Central and Eastern Europe, rarely makes the list. That gap has drawn attention from investors seeking diversification beyond Western Europe. Over the past year, Polish equities have outpaced broad European stocks by a wide margin, and the simplest way for US investors to access that market is through the iShares MSCI Poland ETF (NYSEARCA:EPOL).

EPOL is a single-country emerging market ETF tracking the MSCI Poland IMI 25/50 Index, which covers large, mid, and small-cap Polish equities. Issued by BlackRock iShares and trading since May 25, 2010, the fund holds $643 million in net assets with an expense ratio of 0.59%.

The return engine is straightforward: you are buying into the earnings growth of Polish businesses. Top holdings concentrate in financials, energy, and materials, with PKO Bank Polski, PKN Orlen, KGHM, and Allegro making up a meaningful share. Poland’s domestic consumption has been a durable growth driver, and NATO and EU membership provides institutional credibility that many emerging markets lack. The fund also carries a 2.89% dividend yield, adding a modest income component.

Over the past year, EPOL returned 38.53%, compared to 20.19% for the Vanguard European ETF (NYSEARCA:VGK), which tracks broad developed European markets. Over five years, EPOL is up 127.78%, roughly double VGK’s 60.45%. That is a meaningful gap for a country most US investors have never considered.

Single-country concentration is the primary risk. Poland represents one economy, one currency, and one geopolitical neighborhood. The Polish Zloty trades at roughly 0.27 USD per PLN today, meaning currency moves directly affect returns for US investors. A strengthening dollar erodes gains even when Polish stocks rise in local terms.

Geopolitical proximity to the Russia-Ukraine conflict adds a risk premium that is difficult to quantify but impossible to ignore. Defense spending has surged since 2022, supporting certain sectors while reflecting an elevated threat environment most Western European markets do not carry.

items.t: KGHM Polska Miedz SA Announces CEO Changes
NKT signs EUR 6 billion landmark copper agreement with KGHM
sum: NKT has renewed its long‑term copper supply agreement with leading European mining and smelting company KGHM. The renewed contract secures a stable supply of European‑produced copper for NKT’s power cable manufacturing over the next decade, ensuring long‑term availability through to 2036.

NKT’s copper demand continues to grow in line with the company’s expansion of production facilities to meet the high global demand for power cable solutions. Ensuring access to reliable copper supply sources is therefore essential to maintaining NKT’s competitiveness and strengthening the resilience of its value chain.

Guided by a long‑term perspective on copper market developments, NKT has strengthened its security of supply for the coming decade through the renewed agreement with KGHM. The contract serves as an enabler of NKT’s strategic ambitions of delivering reliably, sustainably and at scale, while reducing the company’s exposure to market fluctuations and geopolitical uncertainty.

- Our extended partnership with KGHM is an important step in securing the long‑term supply of copper that underpins our ability to deliver reliable power cable solutions to our customers. KGHM is a long standing, trusted partner to NKT, consistently demonstrating strong operational performance and high‑quality output. By strengthening this relationship, we reinforce the robustness of our supply chain, reduce our exposure to market volatility and ensure a stable foundation for NKT’s continued growth, says Claes Westerlind, President & CEO of NKT.

KGHM operates across the entire copper value chain, from mining, smelting, refining and recycling to rod manufacturing. By leveraging KGHM’s vertically integrated production capabilities and strong European footprint, NKT secures stable and reliable access to European sourced copper for a significant share of its future requirements, which is especially important given the EU’s strategy to boost resilience by supporting domestic production of critical raw materials as well as the increasing attention paid to the local content.in supply chains.
- Our long‑term cooperation with NKT highlights KGHM’s position as a dependable supplier of high‑quality copper products in a demanding market environment.

items.t: Polish copper miner KGHM dismisses CEO
sum: Polish copper miner KGHM dismissed CEO Andrzej Szydlo and deputy CEO Piotr Stryczek on Friday, the company said in a statement, without providing a reason.
As of 11:22 GMT, shares of the company were down 7.5%, as the leadership overhaul coincided with a sharp correction in copper and precious metal prices.
Analyst Jakub Szkopek from Erste Group said the CEO dismissal was unexpected.
“It will certainly not help KGHM’s share price,” Szkopek said, noting that the change creates uncertainty just as the company was preparing to update its strategy.
The supervisory board has delegated its member Remigiusz Paszkiewicz to temporarily perform the CEO duties for up to three months until a permanent appointment is made, KGHM said.

items.t: Forsee Power to supply battery systems to Polish copper miner KGHM
sum: Polish copper miner KGHM will equip its ZANPER T and HT24e electric mining machines with battery systems from Forsee Power.
KGHM operates copper mines in Europe and manufactures machinery and equipment for the mining sector, including haul trucks, loaders or transport units through its subsidiary KGHM ZANAM.
KGHM ZANAM engineers worked closely with Forsee Power to adapt the battery systems to the demanding conditions of underground mining, Forsee said.

The ZANPER T will be powered by the FORSEE ZEN 54 LITE system. The transport vehicle is designed to operate in non-explosive underground mines. It can transport up to 14 people, including victims from accident sites, as well as transporting materials. The 54 kWh pack in the vehicle’s chassis will provide 100 km of range after a 60-minute charging session, Forsee said.

Forsee Power’s ZEN LITE battery system offers 47 kWh and 54 kWh pack options in a compact format, offering 258 Wh/L energy density. Designed for 350 V powertrains in light and medium trucks, short buses or off-highway vehicles, it can also power 650-800 V heavy vehicles when space is limited.

The ZEN LITE shares the same platform as ZEN PLUS, using nickel manganese cobalt (NMC) cells for flexible charging, either overnight for full operation or fast charging to 50% in under 20 minutes, which is well-suited to fleets with short downtime, according to Foresee.

The electric-powered HT24e shuttle truck will integrate the FORSEE ZEN 36 LFP battery. The HT24e is a low-profile mining haul and dump truck for use in underground workings with limited height. It is designed to haul mined ore and waste rock from the extraction faces to haulage roads in underground mines, especially where headroom is limited.
